w: Torun's Gothic town hall rose in stages across the 13th and 14th centuries, then got rebuilt after damage in the 17th and 18th - one of the finest surviving examples of medieval civic architecture in Central Europe. These days it doesn't govern the town: it houses the District Museum instead.
s: Gothic town hall turned district museum
_facts: Gothic building created in stages during the 13th-14th centuries, reconstructed in the 17th century and rebuilt after 18th-century destruction
one of the most outstanding examples of medieval city architecture in central Europe
main seat of the District Museum in Torun

n: Nicolaus Copernicus native house in Toruń
w: A Gothic tenement house that belonged to the Copernicus family in the second half of the 15th century - and is considered by many historians to be the birthplace of the man who moved the Earth. Whether or not he actually drew his first breath under this roof, it's carried his name and a museum in his honor ever since.
s: Claimed birthplace of the astronomer who moved the Earth
_facts: Gothic tenement house belonging to the Copernicus family in the second half of the 15th century
considered by many historians to be the birthplace of Nicolaus Copernicus
houses a museum dedicated to the astronomer

w: Also known as the Gate of the Holy Spirit, this is one of just three gates of medieval Torun's city walls still standing. Duck through the arch and you're passing the same threshold that once separated the walled town from everything outside it.
s: One of three surviving medieval city gates
_facts: also called the Gate of the Holy Spirit or the Gate of the Lady
one of the three gates of medieval Torun that have survived to this day

n: House Under the Star in Toruń
w: A late-Baroque townhouse crowned with a golden star, from which it takes its name - Kamienica pod Gwiazda. Numerous rebuilds and renovations have reshaped its present form over the centuries, but the star stayed put, making it one of the most distinctive facades on Torun's Old Town market square.
s: Baroque townhouse crowned with a golden star
_facts: distinguished by a late baroque facade decorated at the top with a golden star, from which its name comes
present shape influenced by numerous reconstructions and renovations

w: One of nine defensive towers still standing along Torun's medieval city walls. Plainer than the gates it once guarded beside, the Baszta Zuraw has simply outlasted most of the fortifications it was built to be part of.
s: One of nine surviving medieval wall towers
_facts: one of the nine remaining defensive towers within the city walls of Torun

w: Prussia spent over two decades, from 1872 to 1894, ringing Torun with one of Central Europe's largest fortress systems - built for a war it never had to fight. Its darker chapter came under German occupation in WWII, when it held a POW camp and a prison, and Poles were massacred here as part of the Intelligenzaktion.
s: Prussian fortress turned WWII prison and massacre site
_facts: built in 1872-1894 by the Kingdom of Prussia, one of the largest fortresses in Central and Eastern Europe
did not play a significant role in WWI or later conflicts
in WWII, Germany operated a prison for Poles and the Stalag XX-A POW camp there
site of German massacres of Poles as part of the Intelligenzaktion

w: Records on Dybow Castle stay sparse, but the structure itself endures - protected today as a national Object of Cultural Heritage, a quieter counterpart to the showier Gothic landmarks across Torun's Old Town.
s: A castle protected as national heritage
_facts: a castle in Torun, Poland
a national Object of Cultural Heritage

w: Torun has baked gingerbread since the Middle Ages, and this hands-on museum in an early 19th-century granary puts you to work making it - dough mixed by hand, shaped in traditional molds, under the eye of a costumed 'gingerbread witch' and the master baker. History you can eat, literally.
s: Make gingerbread with a costumed witch and master baker
_facts: hands-on tourist attraction where visitors learn how to make traditional gingerbread using Middle Ages methods and traditional baking molds
located in an early 19th-century granary on Rabianska Street
visitors also participate in flour production using millstones

n: New Town Market Square in Toruń
w: Laid out in 1264, the moment Torun's New Town was founded, this square has anchored the district ever since - a plainer, quieter counterpart to the grander Rynek of the Old Town a short walk away.
s: New Town's market square, laid out in 1264
_facts: the central point of the New Town in Torun, designed in 1264 when the city was founded

w: Poland's puppet-theatre tradition runs deep, and this Torun institution has kept it alive since 1945, founded by Irena Pikiel-Samorewiczowa in the rubble of the war's immediate aftermath. Eight decades on, it's still bringing wood and string to life onstage.
s: Puppet theatre founded amid the rubble of 1945
_facts: a Polish puppet theatre, founded by Irena Pikiel-Samorewiczowa in 1945

w: One of Poland's oldest botanical gardens, planted in 1797 - long before the city had a zoo to go with it. The two merged in 1965, and the combined garden has been a member of the European zoo association since 2007: plants and animals sharing the same green pocket of the city.
s: 1797 botanical garden merged with a zoo in 1965
_facts: botanical garden established in 1797, one of the oldest such gardens in Poland
merged with a newly opened zoo in 1965
member of the European Association of Zoos and Aquaria since 2007
